      "name": "Zen", "vendor": "Mozilla", "version": "1.23.4b", "buildID": "20261020090730",
      "source": "browser.runtime.getBrowserInfo"
    },
    "installed": {
      "name": "Zen", "vendor": "Mozilla", "version": "1.24b", "buildID": "20261029123729",
      "source": "application.ini [App]"
    },
    "process": { "source": "websocket_peer", "mapped_bundle": "backup" },
    "restart_recommended": true,
    "hint": "The connected browser's runtime and installed build differ. Ask the user to save work and restart the browser ..."
  }
}
  • status: "match": runtime and installed Gecko app build IDs agree; restart_recommended: false. It does not prove that page loading is healthy. Product/engine version strings are displayed, never compared against each other; missing or invalid build IDs produce unknown instead.
  • status: "mismatch": those build IDs differ; restart_recommended: true and hint suggest asking the user to save work and restart, then check status and list tabs again. This is evidence of a pending browser restart, not proof of the cause of a page failure.
  • status: "unknown": restart_recommended: null and a reason; not a healthy/matching result.

Runtime metadata is sent by the extension on each connection, not read from page content or a user agent string. Installed-build inspection is currently macOS only. The bridge matches the exact reverse TCP connection of its active extension WebSocket to one PID using lsof, verifies the main executable against its bundle's Info.plist, and reads the current bundle's application.ini. mapped_bundle says current (Contents) or backup (Contents.bak); a backup path alone is not a build mismatch. It never picks a browser by name from the process list or reads a user profile. Each of at most three lsof calls has a one-second timeout, and metadata files are capped at 64 KiB. The peer is rechecked after inspection; a replaced/disconnected extension invalidates the result. The diagnostic returns no paths, PIDs, socket addresses, tokens, or raw subprocess errors.

Unknown reasons include extension_disconnected, runtime_info_unavailable (older extension or runtime metadata not yet received), unsupported_platform (installed-build inspection unavailable), connection_address_unavailable, browser_process_unavailable, ambiguous_browser_process, process_lookup_unavailable (missing helper or access denied), process_lookup_failed, process_lookup_timeout, browser_bundle_unavailable, installed_metadata_unavailable, build_id_unavailable, and connection_changed. A remote/forwarded WebSocket that cannot be tied to a local browser is also unknown, not guessed.

This is read-only: no tabs are opened, navigated, activated or closed; no settings change, extension reload, or browser restart is performed. A bridge predating this option may ignore the query: absence of browser_diagnostics is not a successful build comparison.

docs.title: GET /api/version
docs.text:
Bridge and extension version info. 

{ "bridge": "0.8.1", "api": "1", "extension_connected": true, "extension_version": "0.8.1", "extension_build": "dev", "extension": 25 }

docs.title: Page data (GET, cached 5 s except page-info)
GET /api/page-info
docs.text:
Page metadata plus current dialog policy and recent dialog history. Never cached. Also accepts POST with { "tabId": 123 }. MCP tool: browser_page_info(tab_id=None). 

{ "url": "...", "title": "...", "readyState": "complete", "lang": "en", "width": 890, "height": 992, "forms": 0, "links": 1, "images": 0 }
readyState is the document's document.readyState; see Snapshot readiness. A page that shows a sign-in field or a CAPTCHA adds a needs_user hint.

docs.title: GET /api/page-text
docs.text:
All visible text on the page. 

{ "text": "..." }

docs.title: GET /api/tabs
docs.text:
All open browser tabs. 

{ "tabs": [{ "id": 1, "url": "...", "title": "...", "active": true, "windowId": 1, "index": 0, "owned": true, "mine": true }] }
mine: true marks the tabs the request's X-Kitsune-Owner opened. POST with { "mine": true } returns only those, the most recently opened first (see Tab owners).

docs.title: GET /api/dom
docs.text:
Accessibility tree (depth=6). POST accepts tabId, selector, ref and maxDepth, scoped as in browser_dom. 

{ "tree": { "ref": "s1e0", "tag": "body", "children": [...] }, "refs": 42 }
Sensitive fields report redacted/hasValue instead of value. A tree past the 20,000-char cap also has "truncated": true and a hint.

docs.title: GET /api/forms
docs.text:
All form fields on the page. Sensitive fields have redacted/hasValue instead of value (see Sensitive-field redaction). 

{ "fields": [{ "ref": "e0", "tag": "input", "type": "password", "name": "password", "id": "password", "placeholder": "", "redacted": true, "hasValue": true, "label": "Password", "required": false, "selector": "#password", "bounds": [...] }] }

docs.title: GET /api/screenshot
docs.text:
Captures the active page as PNG and saves to the bridge screenshot directory ($KITSUNE_HOME/screenshots, default ~/.kitsune/screenshots). 

{ "url": "...", "title": "...", "saved_to": "...", "filename": "kitsune_20260313_120000.png" }

docs.title: POST /api/screenshot, /api/element-screenshot, /api/full-page-screenshot
docs.text:
Return dataUrl and capture metadata. Set imagePreview: true for an inline preview under roughly 1 MB (large images are JPEG-encoded and downscaled in the extension). Without that flag, return full PNG data by default, or JPEG with format: "jpeg". Viewport requests accept tabId. Element requests require selector and accept tabId and scale (1–4); full-page requests accept tabId. A capture never shows the tab (tabs.captureTab). Captures retain existing canvas and scroll/segment limits and can truncate very large documents.

MCP tool browser_screenshot(selector=None, full_page=False, tab_id=None, save_to=None, data_url=False, ref=None, element=None, format="png") returns [Image, metadata] by default, giving the model actual MCP image content. save_to writes the full requested PNG/JPEG and returns metadata with saved_to instead. data_url=True returns the raw image data in metadata. Inline preview dimensions can be smaller than the original capture metadata.

docs.title: POST /api/handle-dialog
docs.text:
{ "accept": true, "prompt_text": "answer", "tabId": 123 }

MCP tool: browser_handle_dialog(accept=True, prompt_text=None, tab_id=None). Sets the tab's policy for subsequent dialogs and returns {ok, policy, default, dialogs}. With no policy, default decides (see Page dialogs): "dismiss" in an agent's tab, which dismisses dialogs as accept: false would and records them with auto_dismissed: true; "native" in a user's tab, where the original native alert/confirm/prompt functions run and the user's actual response is recorded. beforeunload keeps native behavior in both. Clear a policy with browser_handle_dialog(accept=None, tab_id=123) or HTTP { "accept": null, "tabId": 123 } to return to the default. Accepted prompts return prompt_text if supplied, otherwise the prompt's default; dismissed prompts return null and dismissed confirms return false. With a policy set, alerts return immediately; in native mode they wait for the user. Recent history is also included in browser_page_info:

{ "policy": { "accept": true, "prompt_text": "answer" }, "default": "dismiss", "dialogs": [
  { "type": "prompt", "message": "Name?", "default_value": "Guest",
    "timestamp": 1792200000000, "response": "answer", "pending": false }
] }

The page-world override records every intercepted invocation (last 100 per document). A native dialog is recorded when it opens, with pending: true until the user answers it. Answers are synchronous; pending: false means the user's native response or automatic answer was already returned, and a later tool call cannot change it. Alert responses are null (no return value). Policies persist across navigation until tab closure or extension restart, with the default applying until asynchronous restoration completes. Clearing a policy also removes it from the per-tab policy store. Capture starts at document_start for new documents and on connection for existing tabs. Scripts holding original references before injection, iframe dialogs (including cross-origin frames), browser-internal pages, and already-open native dialogs are outside this mechanism. Page scripts can also replace or bypass the overrides.

accept: true also disarms beforeunload using the same returnValue/preventDefault suppression as browser_close_tab(force=True), allowing navigation away. Unload events are recorded with type beforeunload. accept: false leaves native unload behavior; the extension cannot answer a native "Leave page?" prompt. Accepting temporarily clears onbeforeunload; clearing or dismissing the policy restores the saved handler if the page has not supplied a replacement. Force-closing remains available regardless of dialog policy.

docs.title: POST /api/wait-for-text
docs.text:
{ "text": "Ready", "text_gone": "Loading", "timeout": 10000, "tabId": 123 }

MCP tool: browser_wait_for(text=...) or browser_wait_for(text_gone=...). Provide at least one non-empty condition (the HTTP endpoint accepts both at once). Polls rendered top-level document text about every 100 ms, excluding hidden text; if both conditions are provided they must both hold. Matching uses case-sensitive substrings. Frames and shadow roots are not traversed. Field names from placeholder, aria-label or aria-labelledby, which snapshots show as names, are not page text and never match. Returns {ok, text, text_gone, elapsed}; timeout returns ok: false with an error. When the text of a timed-out text wait is the name of a visible element, the result also has matched_as: "accessible_name", name_matches (up to 3 {ref, role, name, source}, where source is the attribute) and a hint: act on the ref, or wait for text the page shows. A text wait met by its first read, because the text was already on the page (in a field's label, say), adds already_present: true and a hint (#402). With "new_only": true (browser_wait_for(new_only=True); the core tool's newOnly is accepted but not published), the wait counts the text's occurrences at its start and is met only once more occur. The bridge polls single reads (see browser_wait_for); a zero timeout performs one immediate check.

docs.title: POST /api/navigate
docs.text:
{ "url": "https://example.com", "tabId": 1, "expectTitle": "Example" }

  • tabId is optional and defaults to the active tab.
  • expectTitle is optional. A title that doesn't match returns a warning, which catches silent redirects.
  • User and other clients' tabs return user_tab_read_only without a prompt; the same applies to /api/back, /api/forward and reload. Explicit compatibility opt-outs are described in Protecting your tabs.
  • A load that does not finish in 15 s returns { "ok": false, "timedOut": true, "url": "..." }. If the tab is still about:blank / complete and the page cannot confirm a loaded destination, it also carries code: "navigation_stalled", retryable: false, and the recovery hint of new_tab_stalled (#366). A requested about: URL never gets this code.

docs.title: POST /api/back
docs.text: { "tabId": 1 } goes back in the tab's history and returns { "ok": true, "tabId": 1 } once dispatched. "pageText": true, an internal flag the core browser_navigate_back sends, waits for the page it loads and adds the page's readable snapshot when it fits 2,000 characters (see Post-action snapshots, #448). With KITSUNE_POST_ACTION_SNAPSHOT=0 the flag does nothing.

docs.title: POST /api/new-tab
docs.text:
{ "url": "https://example.com" }. url is optional and defaults to about:blank. Opens an agent-owned tab in the background (it is not shown; see Shared browser). Returns { "ok": true, "tabId": 123 } immediately.

{ "url": "https://example.com", "wait": true, "timeout": 15000 } waits up to timeout ms (default 15000) for the load and returns { "ok": true, "tabId": 123, "url": "https://example.com/after-redirect", "status": "complete" }. On timeout the tab stays open and the result is { "ok": false, "timedOut": true, "tabId": 123, "url": "...", "status": "loading" }. While Zen's first-run welcome screen is open, the browser keeps reporting a loaded tab's URL as about:blank (#360); the wait then asks the page, and url is the page's own URL. With wait, "pageText": true, an internal flag the core browser_tabs action=new url=… sends, adds the loaded page's readable snapshot when it fits 2,000 characters, as a browser_navigate result has it (#448); a larger page, a timeout or KITSUNE_POST_ACTION_SNAPSHOT=0 adds nothing.

If the wait times out with the tab still about:blank / complete, and the page cannot confirm a loaded destination, the result also carries code: "new_tab_stalled", retryable: false, and a hint saying that retrying will not fix it (#366). The tab already exists: tabId is retained (the core browser_tabs returns its index and tab instead). Do not repeat creation or navigation: the browser needs an update, a restart or another fix first. A browser left running after an on-disk update is one possible cause; check browser_status(diagnostics=true) for build mismatch evidence. Tell the user, ask them to save work and restart or update the browser (or fix it another way), and retry only after they say it is fixed. The code describes the observed blank-tab timeout, not a confirmed update mismatch. Kitsune does not restart the browser, activate the tab, or create a replacement automatically. A blank tab requested intentionally still succeeds; a tab still loading retains the ordinary timeout result.

docs.title: POST /api/switch-tab
docs.text: { "tabId": 123 } shows the tab. It switches the user's view, so send it only on the user's request; while the user is using the tab it would hide, it returns user_active.

docs.title: POST /api/close-tab
docs.text: { "tabId": 123, "force": true, "confirmToken": "…" } closes a tab this client may write; any other tab returns user_tab_read_only (see Tab permissions). With a v0.7.1 extension, a tab the agent did not open returns needs_user (user_tab) with a confirm token instead; confirmToken is that token after the user approved. force disarms beforeunload first.

docs.title: POST /api/wake-tab
docs.text:
{ "tabId": 123 } reloads a discarded tab this client may write; reads of a discarded tab of any owner wake it themselves (#449). A tab that is not discarded returns { "ok": true, "woken": false, "discarded": false } at once. Otherwise the call waits up to 15 s for the reloaded page to finish loading and answer the content script, and then returns { "ok": true, "woken": true, "ready": true }; the next command can reach the page. Two results report ready: false:

  • { "ok": true, "woken": true, "ready": false, "unscriptable": true, "state": { "tabId", "url", "status", "title", "httpStatus" } }: the reloaded page loaded but refuses the content script, such as a JSON or PDF viewer or an error response with an empty body. Commands fail with error_page.
  • { "ok": true, "woken": true, "ready": false, "timedOut": true, "state": { "tabId", "url", "status" } }: the page did not become ready within 15 s; state is the last observed state. state.reason: "no_receiver" means the last check found the reloaded page loaded and accepting the content script, but nothing answered its ping. While the page stays silent, commands fail with content_unavailable (state.reason: "no_receiver") before anything is sent.

Ready means the content script answered a ping after the load, not that an injection succeeded. Until the deadline, each check injects and pings again, so a page that starts answering late still ends the wait as ready. Each ping waits at most 1 s; the injection is one browser call whose own duration the deadline cannot cut short.

docs.title: POST /api/click
docs.text:
{ "selector": "button.submit" }. It also accepts ref and position.

The click moves to the target before pressing: pointerover/mouseover, non-bubbling pointerenter/mouseenter on newly entered ancestors and the target, then pointermove/mousemove, sharing browser_hover's pointer tracking. A drag also moves to its source before pressing. The click then dispatches pointerdown, mousedown, pointerup, mouseup and click at the target's center or the given point. For a primary-button press, button: 0; buttons is 0 during approach, 1 at the press and 0 from pointerup on. click is a PointerEvent with detail: 1 and pointerType: "mouse", and it runs the element's native activation once, as el.click() does; a disabled form control gets no click. Limits: every event has isTrusted: false and grants no user activation, and no pointerout or pointerleave is sent. For pages that need trusted input, use browser_trusted_click; an unmet expect whose target is still visible says so in its hint (see Action outcomes).

"holdMs": 600 (0-10000; MCP hold_ms) holds the press for long-press controls (#351): pointerup, mouseup and click (or contextmenu/auxclick) follow that long after pointerdown and mousedown, and the result adds held_ms, the measured hold. The background times the hold, because a hidden tab's page timers fire after 1 s at the earliest; measured in a background tab, a 700 ms hold lasted 729 ms. Any other value returns holdMs must be an integer from 0 to 10000 and dispatches nothing. Add "wait": true, "timeout": 10000 to wait for the target first (see Actionability wait); the other action endpoints accept the same keys.

docs.title: POST /api/trusted-click
docs.text: { "selector": "button.submit", "focus": true } or { "coords": { "x": 640, "y": 400 }, "coordinateSpace": "viewport" }. Optional: tabId, title, process, restorePointer, button (left/right/middle), clickCount (1 or 2), modifiers (["Shift", "Control", "Alt", "Meta"]). OS-level click on Windows, macOS and Linux (X11); see browser_trusted_click. holdMs (0-10000) holds a single click's press. A click that does not finish within 35 s returns a timeout action error with retryable: false.

docs.title: POST /api/trusted-drag
docs.text: { "selector": "#knob", "to": "#mark", "steps": 10 }. Refs work for both ends. Optional: tabId, first, process and focus (false leaves bringing the browser to the front to the caller). OS-level drag on macOS; see browser_trusted_drag. A drag that does not finish within 35 s returns a timeout action error.

docs.title: POST /api/type
docs.text: { "text": "hello", "selector": "input" }

docs.title: POST /api/fill
docs.text:
{ "selector": "input#email", "value": "user@example.com" }

A text field's value is set through the native setter and followed by input and change events, so React and Vue state follows it. A web-component host is filled through the first input, textarea or select in its open or closed shadow root, else in the shadow roots of hosts nested inside it, up to 8 roots deep (closed roots through Firefox's openOrClosedShadowRoot). /api/type, /api/set-editable-content and /api/form-fill use the same lookup. When /api/fill, /api/type or a /api/form-fill key cannot reach a field, the result is a not_fillable action error.

An ARIA slider or spinbutton (role=slider/spinbutton with a numeric aria-valuenow and no native field) has no value to assign, so /api/fill sets it with keys, in the page, in one request (#311): it focuses the target and presses Home or End when the value is aria-valuemin or aria-valuemax, then arrow keys toward the value (ArrowRight/ArrowLeft on a horizontal slider, ArrowUp/ArrowDown on a vertical one or a spinbutton; the other pair when the first does not move it toward the value). Keys are keydown/keyup on the target as /api/keypress dispatches them, a task apart so the page renders each step; a widget that renders only on an animation frame is not waited for, so it looks stuck. The value must be a number; values are compared up to float rounding. It stops at the value: { "ok": true, "tag": "div", "role": "slider", "value": 15, "target": 15, "min": 0, "max": 100, "keys": 35 }. A value outside aria-valuemin/aria-valuemax is a value_not_reached action error (reason: "out_of_range", keys: 0, retryable: true) before any key. When a key steps past the value, a key stops moving it, the arrow keys move it away, or 1,000 keys or 20 s run out, it is a value_not_reached with retryable: false and the same state. A native <input type=range>, also inside a role=slider wrapper, keeps the value setter.

docs.title: POST /api/scroll
docs.text: { "direction": "down", "amount": 500 }. A container selector or ref is optional; element is an audit-only description. loadMore: true marks the scrolls the core browser_find sends for load_more (#447). On a tab this client cannot write, those run only while the tab is not shown (Tab permissions).

docs.title: POST /api/hover
docs.text:
{ "selector": "a.link" }

Returns { "ok": true, "tag": "a" }, plus opened_popup when the hover opened a menu, listbox or dialog.

A selector is scrolled into view first. The hover dispatches, in this order, pointerover, pointerenter, mouseover, mouseenter, pointermove and mousemove at the target's center, as a pointer arriving there would. pointerover, mouseover and the move events go to the target and bubble, across shadow roots (composed: true). pointerenter and mouseenter do not bubble; each goes to every newly entered element from the outermost ancestor to the target, so a row that shows its controls on enter sees the hover of a child. The ancestor chain crosses shadow roots to their hosts and stays within the target's document (in a frame, the <iframe> element is not entered). An ancestor that also contains the element the previous hover pointed at counts as already entered and gets no enter events; the first hover enters every ancestor up to the root element, and so does hovering the same element again, so a retry can reveal what was hidden meanwhile. Kitsune remembers only its own hovers in this document: clicks, the real pointer and browser_trusted_click do not change it, and navigation or reinjection starts over. Pointer events carry pointerType: "mouse", pointerId: 1 and isPrimary, and every event carries view and the point.

Limits: every event has isTrusted: false, and no pointerout, pointerleave, mouseout or mouseleave is sent to the element pointed at before. CSS :hover rules follow only the real pointer, so a control that only a :hover style reveals stays hidden. For it, use browser_trusted_click with restore_pointer=False, which clicks the target with the real pointer and leaves the pointer there, on a target where a click is harmless; or ask the user to point at it.

"durationMs": 400 (0-10000; MCP duration_ms) and "steps": 5 (1-50) keep the pointer moving, for hover-intent controls that wait for several moves over some time (#351). After the hover above, which then arrives at a quarter of the target's width, steps more pointermove/mousemove pairs cross the middle half of the target from left to right at its vertical center, spread evenly over durationMs (5 steps when only durationMs is given), or a task apart without it. The result adds moves (steps + 1) and hovered_ms. As for a held click, the background times the pauses: in a background tab, a 500 ms hover with 5 steps took 579 ms. Values out of range return an error and move nothing.

docs.title: POST /api/drag
docs.text: { "from": "#card", "to": "#done" }, or ref and toRef. Returns { "ok": true, "from": "#card", "to": "#done", "via": "html5" }. It presses the source (pointerdown, mousedown) and dispatches the HTML5 drag events (dragstart … drop, dragend). They count (via: "html5") when the source is draggable, the page let dragstart through and the destination accepted the drop by cancelling dragenter, dragover or drop, as a browser requires. Otherwise the drag is replayed as a pointer drag (via: "pointer") for libraries that build drag on pointer events: ten pointermove/mousemove steps from the source's center to the destination's, so a drag threshold is crossed, each in a new task so the page can render in between; then pointerup and mouseup. Pointer events (pointerId: 1, buttons: 1, isPrimary) go to the source, where setPointerCapture routes them; the page's capture itself is not visible to Kitsune, and Firefox can throw NotFoundError from setPointerCapture for a pointer it has not seen, such as this synthetic one. mouseup lands on the destination.

docs.title: POST /api/find
docs.text:
{ "query": "search text" } or { "selector": "a.link" }

Both query and selector are accepted (normalized to query internally). Returns { "results": [{ "ref": "r0", "tag": "a", "text": "...", "selector": "...", "bounds": [...] }] }. A query that is not a matching CSS selector is split into words (filler words such as "the" or "in" are dropped). Elements are scored per word they match in their text, aria-label, placeholder, title, alt, id, name or value, or a role word ("button", "dropdown", "search bar"), with more for matching every word and for the whole query or a quoted part as a phrase. Only matching elements are returned, best first; when nothing matches, the reply is { "results": [], "hint": "..." }.

docs.title: POST /api/js
docs.text:
{ "code": "document.title" }

Returns { "result": "..." }. A result longer than 8,000,000 characters is cut and marked truncated, with its fullLength. Page JavaScript is not subject to password redaction.

docs.title: POST /api/highlight
docs.text: { "selector": "h1" }. Draws a red border over the element.

docs.title: POST /api/clear-highlight
docs.text: No body needed. Removes all highlights.

docs.title: POST /api/wait-for-element
docs.text:
{ "selector": ".loaded", "timeout": 10000, "pollInterval": 200 }

Polls until the element appears. Returns { "ok": true, "found": true, "ref": "r0", "elapsed": 1200 }; timeout returns ok: false, found: false with an error. The bridge polls single reads (see browser_wait_for); a zero timeout performs one immediate check.

docs.title: POST /api/wait-for-result
docs.text:
{ "code": "document.querySelector('.data')?.textContent", "timeout": 15000, "pollInterval": 500 }

Polls a JavaScript expression until its result is not empty. Returns { "ok": true, "result": "...", "elapsed": 2000, "polls": 4 }.

docs.title: POST /api/page-text-by-tab-id
docs.text: { "tabId": 123 }. Returns the text of that tab, which need not be the active one.

docs.title: POST /api/batch
docs.text:
Execute multiple commands sequentially or in parallel. 

{
  "commands": [
    { "action": "navigate", "url": "https://example.com" },
    { "action": "sleep", "ms": 2000 },
    { "action": "pageText" }
  ],
  "stopOnWarning": false,
  "tabId": 12
}
tabId (optional) is the tab for commands that name none; see Container progress for how steps pick their tab.

Parallel sequences (commands within each sequence run sequentially, sequences run concurrently): 

{
  "commands": [{
    "action": "parallel",
    "sequences": [
      [{ "action": "navigate", "tabId": 1, "url": "https://a.com" }, { "action": "pageText", "tabId": 1 }],
      [{ "action": "navigate", "tabId": 2, "url": "https://b.com" }, { "action": "pageText", "tabId": 2 }]
    ]
  }]
}

Every command that acts on a tab inside parallel sequences needs an explicit tabId, and two sequences may not write the same tab (see Container progress).

Returns { "results": [...], "progress": [...], "status": "ok", "summary": "..." }; progress, status and summary are described in Container progress. When newTab commands, nested ones included, opened tabs that a later closeTab command did not close, newTabs lists their ids, oldest first; the MCP server makes the last one its current tab (No current tab).

A response whose status is not ok adds call and resume_token for POST /api/resume.

Batch actions: navigate, newTab, closeTab, switchTab, click, type, fill, scroll, hover, find, js, pageInfo, pageText, pageTextByTabId, tabs, forms, dom, highlight, screenshot, waitForElement, waitForResult, sleep, parallel, media (see Media).

docs.title: POST /api/resume
docs.text:
Continue a batch, parallel or workflow call that did not finish ok (browser_resume). A direct call's checkpoint is in the MCP server, so this route answers checkpoint_not_found for its call. 

{ "call": 42, "resume_token": "x3J...", "observed": { "1": "not_applied", "0.1.2": "applied" } }
Returns the original call's response shape; see Checkpoint and resume.

docs.title: POST /api/ask-user
docs.text:
The needs_user stop of browser_ask_user (#376); nothing reaches the page. tabId is optional. 

{ "reason": "sign_in", "message": "Sign in to your shop account, please.", "tabId": 12 }
Returns needs_user with state.reason: "agent_request", state.detail (the reason), state.message, the tab's tabId, url and title, state.evidence when the tab shows that hint, and call; see browser_ask_user. Asking the user is the MCP server's.

docs.title: POST /api/needs-user
docs.text:
The needs_user hint a tab shows now, which browser_resume polls (#376). 

{ "tabId": 12 }
Returns { "ok": true, "tabId": 12, "needs_user": { "reason": "sign_in", … } }, with needs_user: null when the tab shows none.

docs.title: GET /api/workflows
docs.text:
List workflow files bundled in the kitsune/workflows package directory. 

{ "workflows": ["gmail-template-draft", "test", "wp-html"], "directory": ".../site-packages/kitsune/workflows" }

docs.title: POST /api/workflow
docs.text:
Execute a named workflow from the workflows directory. 

{ "name": "test", "variables": { "url": "https://example.com" }, "tabId": 12 }
tabId (optional) is the tab for steps that name none. Workflows are .md files with JSON code blocks. Variables use {{name}} syntax. Returns { "workflow": "test", "steps": 4, "results": [...], "progress": [...], "status": "ok", "summary": "..." }, plus newTabs as for POST /api/batch. A workflow stops at its first failed step; progress marks the rest skipped (see Container progress). A workflow that did not finish ok adds call and resume_token for POST /api/resume; resuming is refused if the workflow file changed.

docs.title: History and bookmarks (POST)
docs.text: POST /api/history-search {query, limit?, since?} (since in epoch milliseconds), POST /api/history-visits {url}, and POST /api/bookmarks-search {query, limit?} back the history tools; see History and bookmarks. The bridge adds the policy scope.

docs.title: POST /api/cache
docs.text:
Control the response cache (pageText is cached for 5s by default; tab inventories are always read fresh).

  • Clear the cache: { "action": "clear" }
  • Check its status: { "action": "status" } returns { "entries": 3, "ttl": 5 }
  • Set the TTL: { "action": "ttl", "seconds": 10 }. seconds must be a non-negative number; anything else answers HTTP 400 and keeps the current TTL.

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text:
All endpoints return { "error": "message" } on failure; classified failures add code, retryable, hint, and state (see Action errors). The matching MCP tools mark these results isError: true (see MCP error results). Common errors:

  • "Kitsune extension not connected. Open Firefox or Zen and make sure the Kitsune extension is loaded." (extension_disconnected): the extension is not loaded or the browser is closed
  • "Extension disconnected" (extension_disconnected): the extension dropped during a command; the call fails at once instead of waiting for its timeout
  • "No active tab found" (browser_window_unavailable): there is no normal browser window the extension can use
  • "Command timed out after Ns" (timeout): the extension did not answer in time
  • "Cannot access browser internal page: about:..." (restricted_page): the extension cannot script restricted pages

docs.title: WebArena-Pro four-way, 26 tasks (2026-11-20)
docs.text:
Aside, EgoLite, Playwright MCP and Kitsune on 26 tasks (19 test, 7 dev) from WebArena-Pro (NeurIPS 2026 E&D): multi-step work on 8 self-hosted apps, such as booking the cheapest weekend trip, registering for a course that fits a schedule or replying to every unread email. Two agents, Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5) and Codex (gpt-6.1-sol), one attempt per task: 208 attempts with a 600 s budget each. An attempt passes only with a full score from the task's backend-state and answer checks.

Arm Passed (Claude / Codex) Mean score Tool calls / attempt Input / attempt, incl. cache Median s Kitsune 13/26 / 12/26 0.63 / 0.57 14.0 / 15.8 283k / 414k 59.9 / 70.3 Playwright MCP 13/26 / 12/26 0.64 / 0.57 29.8 / 35.1 660k / 809k 59.9 / 64.0 Aside (CLI REPL) 12/26 / 12/26 0.61 / 0.57 16.1 / 15.6 463k / 512k 67.7 / 58.6 EgoLite (CLI) 12/26 / 12/26 0.61 / 0.59 12.8 / 17.5 360k / 622k 63.9 / 68.5

By split: of the 19 test tasks, Kitsune and Playwright MCP passed 7 under Claude Code and Aside and EgoLite 6; every arm passed 6 under Codex. Every arm passed 6 of the 7 dev tasks under both agents.

Totals on the 12 tasks every arm passed under each agent. They are not the same 12 under both. The percentages are ratios of those totals to Playwright MCP's, not reductions:

Arm Input, incl. cache (Claude / Codex) vs Playwright MCP Tool calls (Claude / Codex) Kitsune 1.08M / 2.76M 39% / 87% 91 / 135 Aside (CLI REPL) 2.76M / 3.13M 99% / 98% 140 / 128 EgoLite (CLI) 2.14M / 3.74M 77% / 117% 94 / 133 Playwright MCP 2.78M / 3.19M 100% / 100% 201 / 258
  • Success was tied. Under each agent all four arms passed the same 12 tasks. Under Claude Code, Kitsune and Playwright MCP passed one more: its answer check needs the flight number, which their answers included and the Aside and EgoLite answers left out.
  • Input: Kitsune used the least under both agents, but by how much depends on the agent and on which attempts count. Per attempt it used 43% of Playwright MCP's input under Claude Code and 51% under Codex. On the tasks every arm passed, where a short failed attempt cannot look cheap, it used 39% and 87%.
  • Tool calls: about half of Playwright MCP's under both agents. Per attempt Kitsune did not make the fewest: EgoLite did under Claude Code and Aside under Codex.
  • Time: no consistent difference. Under Codex, Kitsune had the highest median.
  • Kitsune's problems: navigation to image-heavy pages timed out 7 times under Claude Code and 3 times under Codex, which stopped the script that made it (#561). Under Codex, 9 scripts ran into the 16 KB output limit. In one Claude Code task the agent asked which posts to save instead of saving them.

Limits:

  • One attempt per task and agent; a one-task difference is within noise.
  • Grading has no LLM judge or UI evidence, so a rubric the backend check cannot prove fails. It is stricter than the paper's grading, and these scores are not comparable to its 62.3%. Of the tasks no arm passed, the failing rubric fell through to that judge in 11 of 13 under Claude Code and 12 of 14 under Codex.
  • Browser environments differ: Aside and EgoLite drove the operator's profiles; Playwright MCP and Kitsune ran an isolated headless Firefox.
  • The sites ran in a GitHub codespace over forwarded ports.
  • For CLI arms one tool call is one script that can batch actions. Input counts are usage counters, not billed cost.
  • Four Claude Code attempts, one task that timed out in every arm, have no usage receipt. Their token use is unknown, not zero, so Claude Code's input means and totals cover 25 attempts per arm.

Source: the kitsune-benchmark report and its per-attempt CSV, which has every attempt's status, score, time, tool calls, tool errors and token counts.

docs.title: Four-way, 12 tasks (2026-11-19)
docs.text:
Aside, EgoLite, Playwright MCP and Kitsune on 12 original local web tasks (forms, pagination, a native confirm() dialog, delayed content, shadow DOM, an iframe, a wizard) under two agents: Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5) and Codex (gpt-6.1-sol). One attempt per task, 96 attempts. An attempt passes only if the fixture server received exactly one correct submission.

Arm Passed (Claude / Codex) Tool calls / attempt Input / attempt, incl. cache Median s Kitsune 11/12 / 10/12 3.2 / 2.9 31k / 66k 15.6 / 24.1 Aside (CLI REPL) 12/12 / 12/12 4.7 / 4.8 53k / 79k 24.3 / 35.5 EgoLite (CLI) 12/12 / 11/12 4.0 / 3.5 71k / 76k 17.0 / 22.9 Playwright MCP 12/12 / 10/12 7.1 / 5.9 65k / 93k 17.6 / 32.4
  • Cost: Kitsune made the fewest tool calls and used the least input under both agents. Under Claude Code it used 47% of Playwright MCP's input at 79% of its cost. The order holds on the tasks every arm solved.
  • Kitsune's miss: the native confirm() task, under both agents. The open dialog blocked the click until it timed out, and browser_handle_dialog set a policy for later dialogs instead of accepting the open one.
  • Other tools: EgoLite snapshots do not show checkbox state, so Codex saved the wrong preferences. Aside's one-shot REPL calls lose snapshot refs (22 RefStaleErrors). Playwright MCP had no tool errors; its two Codex misses were Codex stalls.

Limits:

  • One attempt per task and agent; a one-task difference is within noise.
  • Playwright MCP ran an isolated headless Firefox; the other three drove the operator's browser.
  • For CLI arms one tool call is one script that can batch actions. Input tokens are not billed cost.
  • The tasks are small and deterministic: no long navigation, real logins or visual reasoning.

Source: kitsune-benchmark report.

docs.title: Before 2026-11-19
docs.text:
• Four-way comparison (2026-11-13): 23 conditions × 2 repeats under Codex gpt-6.1-sol; every arm completed 46/46. Six-tool Kitsune used 2.9% less input than 14-tool Kitsune, 3.3% less than Aside and 26.3% less than EgoLite, but its adjusted elapsed time was 4.8% and 6.6% higher than 14-tool Kitsune and Aside. Aside used less input in 36/46 paired cells.
  • Five-way MiniWoB (2026-11-12): on 13 shared successful cells, Kitsune's then-default 14 tools used 34.1% less input than Playwright MCP, but 12.4% more than ego lite and 42.6% more than Aside (report).
  • v0.7.2 vs Playwright MCP: Kitsune kept the user's tab in front in 28/28 tasks (Playwright MCP 2/28), cost 0.56–0.97× on tasks both solved, and solved 96/98 tasks (Playwright MCP 98/98) (report).

All reports: kitsune-benchmark.

docs.title: How is it different?
docs.text: If you want to… Consider Hand tasks to an agent in the Firefox-family browser you use, with background tabs and approvals Kitsune Debug or profile pages in Firefox Firefox DevTools MCP Test across Chromium, Firefox and WebKit in browsers it launches Playwright MCP Drive the Chrome you already use A Chromium extension MCP such as Browser MCP

docs.title: Checkpoint and resume
docs.text: A browser_batch, browser_parallel or browser_workflow call that did not finish ok, or a direct call that stopped on needs_user, can be continued with browser_resume. One rule holds: a resume never resends a write that ran ok, and resends a write whose outcome is unknown only after the caller observed that it did not take effect.

docs.title: Checkpoints
docs.text:
A container call whose status is not ok keeps a checkpoint, and its response adds call and resume_token to results, progress, status and summary (Container progress):

{ "results": [{ "ok": true }, { "error": "Command timed out after 30s", "code": "timeout", "retryable": false }],
  "progress": [
    { "index": 0, "action": "click", "tabId": 3, "status": "ok" },
    { "index": 1, "action": "submitForm", "tabId": 3, "status": "unknown" },
    { "index": 2, "action": "pageText", "tabId": 3, "status": "skipped" }],
  "status": "unknown",
  "call": 42,
  "resume_token": "x3J..." }
  • Resuming needs both call (the audit call id) and the random resume_token.
  • Checkpoints live in bridge memory only (never on disk or in the audit log): at most 20, each expiring 30 minutes after its call. A bridge restart loses them. Only a hash of the token is kept.

docs.title: browser_resume
docs.text:
browser_resume(call, resume_token, observed=None, wait=120)

The response has the shape of the original call. If it still did not finish ok, it carries the same call and a new resume_token; the old token stops working. A container resume has a fixed 300 s deadline.

docs.title: Step paths
docs.text: Path Step "2" top-level command 2 "0.1.3" step 3 of sequence 1 of the parallel at command 0 "1.2" step 2 of the sequence at command 1

docs.title: What each step does
docs.text:
Last record Resume ok Not sent; its result is reused (resumed: "kept"). An ok read in a sequence reruns if a later step uses its result via ${$N...} skipped Sent failed Sent again held Sent again through ask-before-act, so it stays held while ask mode is on. Report it "applied" after confirming it directly unknown read Sent again unknown write Refused until observed reports "not_applied" (resend) or "applied" (mark ok)

Writes include the bridge's write actions, agent JavaScript, cookies, storage, clipboard, downloads, broadcast, navigate, newTab, closeTab and switchTab. sequence and parallel resume step by step; other blocks (if, while, try, retry, broadcast) resume as one step, and one containing a write that ran ok accepts only "applied".

observed maps step paths to "applied" or "not_applied", for unknown, held and failed steps only. Every resumed step passes the current policy again; confirmation tokens are never honored inside a resume.

docs.title: Workflows
docs.text: A workflow checkpoint keeps the file's SHA-256; a changed file is refused with workflow_changed. Batch and workflow checkpoints keep the call's default tab.

docs.title: Parallel
docs.text: Sequences each continue from their own records. A sequence is refused (nothing sent) with tab_closed if a tab it needs was closed, tab_owned if another sequence claimed a tab it writes, or tab_claimed if another running parallel writes it.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
All except resume_failed send nothing and keep the checkpoint.

code HTTP Meaning checkpoint_not_found 404 Finished ok, expired, pushed out, being resumed, or the bridge restarted resume_token_invalid 403 Not the latest token workflow_changed 409 The workflow file changed observed_invalid 400 observed names a step that cannot take it, or an invalid value (state.steps) observed_required 400 A step needs an observation (state.steps) resume_failed 200 Internal error; progress reports what ran and the checkpoint is dropped

docs.title: Audit log
docs.text: Resumed steps are audited with parent: {call, path, resumed: true} (Audit log). The token never appears in any log.

docs.title: Direct calls
docs.text:
A direct call that stops on needs_user unresolved (an approval hold without elicitation, a declined or unanswered approval prompt, or a browser_ask_user request) adds call and resume_token to its result. Tab handoff requests and tools without confirm_token get no checkpoint.

The MCP server that made the call keeps the checkpoint in memory under the same limits (20, 30 minutes). Another client or a restarted server cannot resume it.

browser_resume(call, resume_token, wait=120) reruns the tool from the held request:

  • Nothing that ran ok is resent. browser_fill_form skips fields filled before the hold; browser_type(submit=true) held at Enter only presses Enter.
  • It grants nothing a new call wouldn't. The request passes the current policy and tab permissions again; if the hold no longer applies, it runs.
  • It never waits for a hold to lift. With elicitation, a renewed hold is asked about for up to wait seconds (wait=0 asks nothing). Without elicitation it returns needs_user again at once with a new token.
  • wait is 0–300 seconds. For sign_in and human_check stops, the resume polls the tab every second until the needs_user hint is gone.

browser_ask_user keeps a checkpoint when the prompt was dismissed or unanswered, or, without elicitation, when the tab showed a sign_in/human_check hint; the resume asks again or waits for the hint to clear.

code Meaning current_tab_changed The agent made another tab current; select it again or call the tool again observed_invalid observed was given; direct calls have no steps resume_token_invalid Not the latest token

docs.title: Without browser_resume
docs.text: Once a checkpoint is gone, send a new batch starting at the first record that is not ok (after checking the page for unknown ones), or call the direct tool again.

docs.text:
Variable Default Meaning KITSUNE_SCRIPTING 1 1: the 6 default tools, including browser_run_python (local Python, not a sandbox). 0: the legacy tool list without Python KITSUNE_HOME ~/.kitsune Data directory (0700) KITSUNE_HTTP_PORT 47651 Bridge HTTP API KITSUNE_WS_PORT 47652 Extension WebSocket. Change WS_URL in extension/background/background.js too KITSUNE_TOKEN Unset Override the token in ~/.kitsune/token KITSUNE_EXTENSION_DIR extension/ in a checkout Developer build the bridge checks for unreloaded edits (Connection diagnosis) KITSUNE_NO_BRIDGE_RESTART Unset 1: don't replace an outdated bridge automatically KITSUNE_BRIDGE_IDLE_TIMEOUT 0 (never) Seconds without activity before the bridge exits (Idle shutdown) KITSUNE_OUTPUT_DIR Unset Directory for relative filename arguments; else the client's first root, else the server's working directory KITSUNE_OWNER_ID The MCP client's process Tab owner id (up to 64 of [A-Za-z0-9._:-]). Set it when the server runs through a launcher other than uv/uvx. Clients with the same value share tabs (Tab owners) KITSUNE_USER_TABS read-only writable lets this client write your tabs (Protecting your tabs) KITSUNE_ASK_BEFORE_ACT Unset 1 starts the bridge with ask-before-act locked on KITSUNE_HISTORY_ALLOW_DOMAINS Unset (all) Comma-separated domains the history tools may return (History and bookmarks) KITSUNE_HISTORY_DENY_DOMAINS Unset Domains the history tools never return; wins over the allow list KITSUNE_HISTORY_MAX_DAYS 30 How far back history tools may look. browser_set_policy can only tighten these three KITSUNE_POST_ACTION_SNAPSHOT Deltas Bridge: 0 disables post-action snapshots, full returns full ones, text adds readable text (details)

The removed KITSUNE_CAPS, KITSUNE_PUBLISH and KITSUNE_MODE make the server refuse to start; delete them. Approvals are set in the extension's options instead.

File Content token Bearer token for the HTTP API (0600) bridge.log Daemon output sessions/ Saved sessions, including cookies screenshots/ Screenshots ask-before-act-locked Present while ask-before-act is locked on; delete it to unlock

docs.title: Setup from a checkout
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/junyeong-nero/kitsune ~/workspace/kitsune
cd ~/workspace/kitsune
uv sync

Register the checkout so the client runs your working tree:

claude mcp add --scope user kitsune -- uv run --directory ~/workspace/kitsune kitsune

In JSON or TOML configs, use "command": "uv" with ["run", "--directory", "/Users/you/workspace/kitsune", "kitsune"]. Load the extension from extension/manifest.json (the developer build). For the signed variant:

uv run python scripts/build_extension.py signed   # then load build/extension-signed/manifest.json

To test the installed-package path, build both wheels and run from them:

uv build --all-packages
uvx --from dist/kitsune_browser_mcp-<version>-py3-none-any.whl \
    --with dist/kitsune_browser-<version>-py3-none-any.whl kitsune

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests -q
for test in tests/*.cjs; do node "$test"; done

Python tests cover the MCP tool surface, snapshots, waits and the bridge; the Node harnesses cover content-script behavior. For an end-to-end check, follow Try it with the extension loaded. Bug reports should include the browser version, browser_status's build, the tool calls and expected versus actual behavior, on a minimal page with secrets redacted.

docs.title: Tool definition budgets
docs.text:
Tool definitions are resent with every model request, so their size is tracked. uv run python scripts/tool_schema_size.py reports each tool's compact JSON size; a test fails until --update records changes in tests/tool_schema_sizes.json, and when totals exceed the budgets in that script. Raise a budget only deliberately.

Conventions the tests enforce:

  • The core tools are Playwright MCP's, published verbatim from src/kitsune/playwright_tools.json (tests/test_playwright_tools.py).
  • Kitsune-owned schemas omit pydantic titles and publish optional parameters as plain types without null/"" defaults; calls are still validated by pydantic (tests/test_tool_schema_titles.py, tests/test_tool_schema_optionals.py).
  • Parameters are documented in the schema (Annotated[..., Field(description=...)]), not in Args: blocks. A tool's first paragraph says what it does; the shared action contract (ref, element, wait, expect, confirm_token, first) is documented once on browser_check (tests/test_tool_first_paragraph.py).

docs.title: Real-browser suites
docs.text:
tests/test_real_browser*.py run against a real Firefox, Zen or LibreWolf and are skipped unless KITSUNE_E2E_BROWSER names the binary:

KITSUNE_E2E_BROWSER=/Applications/Zen.app/Contents/MacOS/zen \
  uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_real_browser*.py' -v

Use -p <file> to run one suite. Each class starts a headless browser on a temporary profile with its own bridge and fixture site on spare ports; your profiles and bridge are untouched. See tests/real_browser_harness.py for adding a suite.

Set KITSUNE_E2E_ARTIFACTS=/some/dir to keep evidence from failures: each failing test writes a directory with a timeline.jsonl (bridge requests, fixture requests and navigation events on one clock), tails of browser.log and bridge.log (tokens redacted), resources.json and summary.json.

docs.title: Website
docs.text:
GitHub Pages serves the landing page (landing/) at junyeong-nero.github.io/kitsune and these docs under /docs/. A push to main that touches either deploys both (.github/workflows/docs.yml).

uv run --group docs mkdocs serve                        # docs only, live reload
uv run --only-group docs python scripts/build_site.py   # landing + docs + redirects in _site/
python -m http.server -d _site

The docs used to live at the site root, so build_site.py writes a redirect page at each old path. The landing page's copy follows README.md; update both together.

docs.text: MIT. See LICENSE.

docs.title: How is it different from Playwright MCP?
docs.text: Playwright MCP launches its own browser, which suits testing. Kitsune attaches to the Firefox, Zen or LibreWolf window you already use and shares it with you: agent tabs open in the background and your tabs are read-only to the agent. With KITSUNE_SCRIPTING=0 it publishes Playwright MCP's 25 core tools unchanged, so prompts carry over. See the benchmark.

docs.title: How is it different from Firefox DevTools MCP?
docs.text: Firefox DevTools MCP is better for debugging and profiling and needs a Firefox started with remote-debugging flags. Kitsune uses an extension, so your normal profile needs no flags or WebDriver.

docs.title: Does it work with Chrome?
docs.text: Not yet. For Chrome, try a Chromium extension MCP such as Browser MCP.

docs.title: Which agents can use it?
docs.text: Any MCP client that runs local stdio servers. See Register the MCP server.

docs.title: Will the agent take over the tab I'm using?
docs.text: No. Its tabs open in the background, and selecting a tab doesn't change what you see. It can read every tab, but writes, navigation, scrolling and closing on your tabs fail with user_tab_read_only unless you hand the tab over. OS-level clicks and site popups can still take focus (Shared browser).

docs.title: Can I limit what the agent does?
docs.text:
• Choose which tools need approval in the extension's options (cookies, storage, clipboard and history do by default).
  • Your tabs stay read-only unless KITSUNE_USER_TABS=writable.
  • Ask-before-act holds submits, payment pages, JavaScript and cookie access until you approve.

docs.title: How do I approve a held action?
docs.text: Clients with elicitation (Claude Code, Codex) ask you in their own prompt. Others fall back to a confirm_token: the agent asks you, then repeats the call with it. See Approving held actions.

docs.title: Is it safe to give an agent my browser?
docs.text: Treat it as giving the agent your signed-in accounts. Nothing in Kitsune prevents prompt injection. Use a dedicated profile with only the accounts the task needs. See Security.

docs.title: Does my data leave my machine?
docs.text: The bridge listens only on 127.0.0.1 and requires a token. Page content the agent reads goes to your agent and its model provider.

docs.title: Do I need the developer build?
docs.text: Only for agent JavaScript (browser_evaluate). The signed build installs once and updates itself. See Installation.

docs.title: Which platforms are supported?
docs.text: macOS and Linux. Trusted OS clicks work on macOS and on Linux under X11.

docs.title: Why can't the agent open "Continue with Google"?
docs.text: Firefox blocks sign-in popups from synthetic clicks. Have the agent ask you to click, or use browser_trusted_click. See Sign-in popups.

docs.title: Is this kitsune-mcp?
docs.text: No, that is an unrelated project. This one is kitsune-browser-mcp on PyPI and io.github.junyeong-nero/kitsune in the MCP Registry.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
agent ──stdio──▶ kitsune (MCP server, one per agent)
                    │ HTTP 127.0.0.1:47651 + bearer token
                    ▼
                 bridge daemon (one per user, started on demand)
                    │ WebSocket 127.0.0.1:47652, moz-extension:// origin only
                    ▼
                 Kitsune extension ──▶ tabs (content scripts)
  1. The agent launches kitsune over stdio.
  2. If no bridge answers, kitsune starts one as a detached daemon, replacing a bridge of a different build. A file lock serializes starts across agents.
  3. The extension reconnects to the daemon by itself; the first tool call after a start waits up to 16 s for it.
  4. The daemon outlives the agent; the next agent reuses it.

docs.title: Snapshots and refs
docs.text:
A snapshot is a compact accessibility-style tree of the page:

- main ""
  - heading "Welcome" [ref=e0] [level=1]
  - button "Log in" [ref=e1]

Actions take a ref (e1) or a selector. A write's selector must match one element, else ambiguous_target, unless first=True (Strict selectors).

Refs stay valid while their node stays attached in the same document, across later snapshots. Navigation, node replacement or an extension reload invalidates them; a stale ref reports element_removed, not_in_snapshot or other_document. Take a new snapshot, and never repeat a write just to refresh refs (Ref lifetime).

Actions return a post-action snapshot (at most 4,000 characters). Clicks, typing and similar actions return a delta: the target and what changed, with - removed: … lines for closed parts. A click that opens a menu or dialog also returns opened_popup with its items' refs (Opened popups). Submits and navigations return a full snapshot. KITSUNE_POST_ACTION_SNAPSHOT in the bridge environment changes this (Post-action snapshots).

browser_snapshot(text=True) adds visible text, URL and title in one bounded call. The tree is built from the DOM, not Firefox's accessibility tree; shadow roots and iframes, including cross-origin ones, are read and acted on (Frames).

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Kitsune has two parts: an MCP server that your agent starts for you, and a browser extension you install once. Setup takes four steps.

Before you start

  • macOS or Linux
  • Firefox 142+, Zen 1.23+ or LibreWolf
  • An MCP client: Claude Code, Codex CLI, Pi, Claude Desktop, Cursor or OpenCode

docs.title: 1. Install uv
docs.text:
uv downloads and runs the Kitsune server. It provides uvx and Python 3.10+. Skip this step if uvx --version already works.

Installer scriptHomebrew 
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

brew install uv

Open a new terminal, then download Kitsune once to check that it runs:

uvx --from kitsune-browser-mcp kitsune-bridge status

It prints "status": "stopped". That is expected: your agent starts the bridge later.

The package is kitsune-browser-mcp

kitsune-mcp is an unrelated project.

docs.title: 2. Install the browser extension
docs.text:
Open the latest release

  1. Download kitsune-<version>.xpi from the release's Assets list.
  2. In Firefox, Zen or LibreWolf, type about:addons in the address bar and press Enter.
  3. Click the gear icon, then Install Add-on From File…, and pick the .xpi file.
  4. Click Add when the browser asks.
  5. Pin Kitsune to the toolbar: click the Extensions (puzzle) button, then the gear next to Kitsune, then Pin to Toolbar. Tab handoff requests and tool approvals show up in its popup.

This is the signed build. It installs once and updates itself. Use the extension from the same release as the server; uvx runs the latest release unless you pin a version. If your agent needs to run its own JavaScript in pages, use the developer build instead.

docs.title: 3. Add Kitsune to your agent
docs.text:
Pick your client. Every client runs the same command, uvx --from kitsune-browser-mcp kitsune; only where you put it differs.

Claude CodeCodex CLIPiClaude DesktopCursorOpenCode

Run once:

claude mcp add --scope user kitsune -- uvx --from kitsune-browser-mcp kitsune

Then start a new Claude Code session. To set an environment variable, add -e before the --, for example -e KITSUNE_SCRIPTING=0.

Run once:

codex mcp add kitsune -- uvx --from kitsune-browser-mcp kitsune

Then start a new Codex session. Or add it to ~/.codex/config.toml yourself:

[mcp_servers.kitsune]
command = "uvx"
args = ["--from", "kitsune-browser-mcp", "kitsune"]

[mcp_servers.kitsune.env]  # optional
KITSUNE_SCRIPTING = "0"

Run once:

pi mcp add kitsune -- uvx --from kitsune-browser-mcp kitsune

This writes ~/.pi/agent/mcp.json (--local writes .pi/mcp.json). In a running session, type /reload.

Add this to ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json (macOS), merging it with any mcpServers already there:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "kitsune": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["--from", "kitsune-browser-mcp", "kitsune"]
    }
  }
}

Quit and reopen Claude Desktop. If it can't find uvx, replace "uvx" with the full path that which uvx prints: apps started from the Dock don't see your shell's PATH. Add "env": {...} next to args for environment variables.

Add this to ~/.cursor/mcp.json, merging it with any mcpServers already there:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "kitsune": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["--from", "kitsune-browser-mcp", "kitsune"]
    }
  }
}

Restart Cursor. If it can't find uvx, replace "uvx" with the full path that which uvx prints. Add "env": {...} next to args for environment variables.

Add this to ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json, or to a project's opencode.json:

{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "mcp": {
    "kitsune": {
      "type": "local",
      "command": ["uvx", "--from", "kitsune-browser-mcp", "kitsune"],
      "enabled": true
    }
  }
}

Then restart OpenCode.

Using more than one client? They share one bridge, so register them all with the same source and version (compatibility).

docs.title: 4. Check that it works
docs.text:
1. Keep the browser open and start a new session of your agent.
  2. Ask it: "List my open browser tabs." It should answer with the tabs you have open.
  3. Click the Kitsune icon in the toolbar. The popup says Connected.

Next, try a first task.

It doesn't work

Check the bridge from a terminal:

uvx --from kitsune-browser-mcp kitsune-bridge status
  • "status": "stopped": the agent hasn't started Kitsune. Check step 3 and restart the agent.
  • "extension_connected": false: the extension isn't connected. Check that it is installed and enabled in about:addons, and that the browser is open.
  • "extension_connected": true: the setup works. If a tool call still fails, its error's hint says what to fix.

More in Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Developer build
docs.text:
Only needed if your agent should run its own JavaScript in pages (browser_evaluate, JavaScript batch conditions), which Mozilla's policy keeps out of the signed build.

Signed (kitsune-<version>.xpi) Developer (kitsune-extension-dev-<version>.zip) Install Once; updates itself Temporary; load it again after every browser restart Agent JavaScript No Yes
  1. Download and unzip kitsune-extension-dev-<version>.zip (or use extension/ from a checkout).
  2. Open about:debugging#/runtime/this-firefox, click Load Temporary Add-on… and pick its manifest.json.

Both builds share an add-on ID; a loaded developer build replaces the signed one until restart. browser_status reports which one is connected as extension_build (signed or dev).

docs.title: Pinning a version
docs.text:
claude mcp add --scope user kitsune -- uvx --from kitsune-browser-mcp==0.8.1 kitsune

For an unreleased commit, tag or branch, use the Git source and get the extension from the same ref:

claude mcp add --scope user kitsune -- uvx --from "git+https://github.com/junyeong-nero/kitsune.git@<ref>#subdirectory=packages/kitsune-browser-mcp" kitsune

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
Server. uvx keeps using its cached version. Refresh it, then reconnect the client:

uvx --refresh --from kitsune-browser-mcp kitsune-bridge status

Or register kitsune-browser-mcp@latest to check on every start. For pinned versions, change the version in the client config. In a checkout: git pull && uv sync.

Bridge. The MCP server restarts a bridge whose build differs from its own, briefly interrupting other clients; KITSUNE_NO_BRIDGE_RESTART=1 opts out. Manage it manually with kitsune-bridge status / stop (from the same source as your clients).

Extension. The signed build updates itself; install a new XPI to update right away. Reload the developer build in about:debugging. A bridge restart does not reload extension code; reload existing tabs if their content scripts are outdated.

docs.title: Idle shutdown (opt-in)
docs.text: Set KITSUNE_BRIDGE_IDLE_TIMEOUT (seconds) in the MCP server environment, or run kitsune-bridge start --idle-timeout SECONDS, to stop the bridge after inactivity. Each HTTP call counts as activity; the timer pauses while a request, extension command or browser_keep_alive loop is running. The next tool call starts a fresh bridge. The first server to start the bridge decides the timeout.

docs.title: Automatic extension updates
docs.text: The signed build checks https://github.com/junyeong-nero/kitsune/releases/latest/download/updates.json about once a day (about:addons → gear → Check for Updates to check now). The extension can then be newer than a cached server; browser_status shows extension_version differing from bridge_version until you refresh the server. If you pin an old server, turn off automatic updates for Kitsune.

docs.title: Extension and server compatibility
docs.text:
• Install the server and extension from the same release or ref; they are tested only together.
  • Use one install source for all clients. A checkout's build hashes its extension/ files and differs from a uvx install of the same commit, so mixed clients keep replacing the bridge. To mix sources anyway, set KITSUNE_NO_BRIDGE_RESTART=1 and manage the bridge yourself.

docs.title: Trusted clicks on macOS
docs.text: For browser_trusted_click on macOS, use kitsune-browser-mcp[macos] or install cliclick (Trusted clicks).

docs.title: Running from a checkout
docs.text: See Development.

docs.title: Philosophy
docs.text: Two principles decide Kitsune's trade-offs. When a feature conflicts with them, the principles win.

docs.title: 1. The user's browser belongs to the user
docs.text:
The agent is a guest in a browser someone is using.

  • Agent work opens in background tabs; the user's view stays where it is.
  • User tabs, focus and input are off-limits unless the user allows otherwise.
  • Refuse with guidance rather than silently act somewhere else.
  • Don't buy speed with interference, and document where protections have limits.

docs.title: 2. Fewer, sharper tools
docs.text:
Every tool and description line costs agent context on every call.

  • Keep the default surface small and each contract precise.
  • Enforce limits (approvals, protected tabs) in the system, not in prompts.
  • Report what happened (dispatched, observed or unknown) and let the agent decide.
  • Add a tool or field only when it removes more agent work than it adds.

docs.title: Python API
docs.text:
The kitsune package drives the browser you already have open from Python, through the same extension and bridge as the MCP server. The MCP server gives an agent a small tool surface; the Python API reaches every capability, storage and history included. Both follow the same shared-browser rules.

pip install kitsune-browser      # or: uv add kitsune-browser

It needs the Kitsune extension (Installation). Keep scripts on the same version as your MCP clients, since they share one bridge.

import kitsune

browser = kitsune.connect()                        # starts the bridge if none runs
tab = browser.new_tab("https://news.ycombinator.com")   # a background tab
for link in tab.query(".titleline > a", fields=["text", "href"], limit=3):
    print(link["text"], link["href"])
tab.close()

docs.title: Connecting
docs.text:
kitsune.connect() starts the shared bridge if needed, waits for the extension and returns a Browser; it raises ConnectionFailed if the extension is not connected.

Argument Default Effect user_tabs read-only writable lets this client write your tabs (Protecting your tabs) confirm None Decides on held actions; see Ask-before-act replace_bridge False Replace a running bridge of another build (which drops its clients' state)

KITSUNE_HTTP_PORT, KITSUNE_TOKEN and KITSUNE_HOME choose the bridge (Configuration). A bridge of another build raises ConnectionFailed (bridge_version_mismatch).

An application that already owns a BridgeClient can wrap it with Browser(existing_client), keeping its identity and permissions. Browser is an API wrapper, not a sandbox.

docs.title: Python scripting through MCP
docs.text:
browser_run_python(code, timeout=30) is one of the default tools. It runs ordinary local Python with host file, environment, subprocess and network access: not a sandbox. Approvals and tab protection apply to the supplied browser API, not to arbitrary code. Set KITSUNE_SCRIPTING=0 for clients you don't trust with local code.

for target, value in {"#name": "Ada", "#note": "Please review."}.items():
    tab.fill(target, value)
result = tab.snapshot()
  • browser is the API, routed through the MCP session. Don't call kitsune.connect().
  • tab is the MCP-selected tab at start, else the tab you are viewing. Scripts don't change the MCP selection. browser.tabs() returns dicts with real tab ids (not MCP list indexes); wrap one with browser.tab(t["id"]).
  • Each run has fresh variables and a temporary working directory; tabs persist. No top-level await.
  • Return data with print(...) or a JSON-compatible result. Intermediate reads are not sent to the model. Use browser_take_screenshot for images.
  • Limits: 64,000 bytes of code; 16,000 bytes of output and result combined (bytes, not characters); 100 API calls; 30 s default deadline, 120 s max.
  • A failed API call stops the script, even if caught. Earlier writes stay applied: observe the page and run only the remaining work, never replay the script. An approval stop names a recovery_tool for browser_tools_call. A tool you require approval for pauses the script instead, without counting against the deadline.
  • On timeout the worker is killed; a command already sent may still finish, so read the page before writing again.
  • help(tab.query) prints a method's signature.

Keep output bounded on long pages: read a known region or a bounded index first, then a scoped snapshot of the section you found.

links = tab.query("nav a[href]", fields=["text", "href"], limit=200)
matches = [l for l in links if "delivery" in l.get("text", "").casefold()]
result = {"matches": matches[:5], "more": len(matches) > 5}

On script_output_limit the output is incomplete: make a new, smaller read-only observation.

docs.title: Tabs
docs.text:
Browser method Returns tabs() list[dict]: id, url, title, active, windowId, index, owned new_tab(url="about:blank", wait=True, timeout=15000) A Tab for a new background tab. A slow load raises TimedOut; the tab id is in error.result["tabId"] tab(tab_id) A Tab for an existing tab active_tab() The tab you are viewing (ambiguous_target with several windows) Tab method Does close(force=False) Close this client's tab; force disarms beforeunload show() Switch your view to the tab wake() Reload a discarded tab duplicate() A background copy pin(), mute(), zoom(), set_zoom(factor) Tab state move(window_id=None, index=-1), detach(), resize_window(width, height) Placement tag(name) Name the tab; browser.tags.tab(name), .list(), .remove(name)

browser.windows: list(), create(url=None, incognito=False), close(id), focus(id). browser.pool: create(size, url), acquire(), release(tab).

docs.title: Reading
docs.text:
Tab method Returns text() Visible text snapshot(target=None, *, max_depth=None, text=False) Accessibility-style tree with refs (Snapshots) markdown(target=None) The page or a subtree as Markdown html(target) One element's outerHTML ("html" for the page) query(selector, fields=None, limit=50) Fields of matching elements (max 500 rows, 400-char snippets); warns when truncated find(query) Elements matching a description like "login button", best first forms() Form fields with labels and values links(internal_only=False) Links info() URL, title, readyState, sizes, scroll, recent dialogs screenshot(path=None, target=None, full_page=False, format="png") Image bytes, optionally written to path evaluate(function, target=None) A JS function's JSON result (developer build). Page globals via window.wrappedJSObject dom(target=None, max_depth=None) Interactive elements as nested dicts images(), iframes(), meta(), structured_data(), readability() Images, frames, meta tags, JSON-LD/Open Graph, main article

Sensitive values are redacted (Sensitive-field redaction). Reads cut at the bridge's caps warn with a UserWarning; pass a target to read less.

docs.title: Selector contract by method
docs.text:
Method CSS Ref (e12) Playwright-style Matching Actions (click, fill, …) Yes Yes Yes Strict: ambiguous matches are refused snapshot(target) Yes Yes Yes First match query(selector) Yes No No Current document only wait_for(target=) Yes Yes No First visible match

tab.find(query) is not browser_find: it has no text/regex arguments. For literal or regex matching, filter a scoped read in Python:

import re
lines = tab.snapshot("main", text=True).splitlines()
result = [line for line in lines if re.search(r"원|USD", line)][:10]

docs.title: Inspecting
docs.text:

docs.title: Editing and focus
docs.text: fill replaces a value; type appends (or inserts at the caret in contenteditable). For a caret-sensitive edit in a native field, use press with a character. press(target=...) dispatches to that element without focusing it; without a target it uses the current focus. Check the result's effect and prevented, and read the page, rather than trusting ok.

docs.text:
tab.wait_for(...) waits up to timeout ms (default 10000) for one condition, else TimedOut:

Condition Holds when target= The first CSS or ref match is visible text=, text_gone= Rendered text contains, or no longer contains, the literal text url=, title= URL or title matches a JS regex js= An expression returns a non-empty result (developer build) network_idle=True No new resource for 500 ms

docs.title: Batches, parallel tabs and workflows
docs.text:
browser.batch(commands, tab=None) runs batch commands in one request, browser.parallel(sequences) runs one sequence per tab, and browser.workflow(name, variables) runs a named workflow (browser.workflows() lists them). Failures don't raise: see results and progress. An unfinished call returns call and resume_token for browser.resume(...) (Checkpoint and resume). browser.retry(command, max_attempts=3) retries retryable failures.

browser.keep_alive(tabs) / stop_keep_alive() prevent tab unloading, browser.broadcast(tabs, command) runs a command in each tab, and browser.sync_barrier(tabs, predicate) waits for a JS predicate in all of them.

docs.title: Ask-before-act
docs.text:
With ask-before-act on, held actions raise ConfirmationRequired. Repeat the call with confirm=error.token within error.expires_in seconds, or pass a confirm function to connect() that decides and returns True to resend:

def ask(held):
    return input(f"{held} -- allow? [y/N] ").strip().lower() == "y"

browser = kitsune.connect(confirm=ask)

User-tab writes fail with user_tab_read_only instead; tokens don't override tab permissions.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
The bridge protects against:

  • Web pages calling the local API. The HTTP API needs a bearer token and sends no CORS headers.
  • DNS rebinding. Requests with a Host other than 127.0.0.1/localhost are rejected.
  • Pages posing as the extension. The WebSocket accepts only moz-extension:// origins.

It does not protect against:

  • Prompt injection. A page can contain instructions, and the agent acts with every account you are signed into.
  • Local processes running as your user, which can read the token.
  • Python scripting. browser_run_python (on by default) runs local Python with host file, network and environment access. It is not a sandbox: code can bypass the browser API. Require approval for it in the extension's options, or set KITSUNE_SCRIPTING=0 for clients you don't trust with local code.
  • Sensitive page data. Read tools redact passwords, one-time codes, card numbers, secret-named, masked and autofilled fields (Sensitive-field redaction), but detection is heuristic and browser_evaluate can read anything the page can.
  • Typed values outside the bridge. The audit log redacts typed text and stored secrets (Audit log), but the page and the client's transcript see them.
  • Cookies, storage, sessions and the clipboard. These tools need your approval by default; lift it only for agents you trust with your accounts.
  • History and bookmarks. Off until you allow it in Kitsune's options. Lookups are scoped (30 days by default), redact token-like URL values and are audited (History and bookmarks).
  • Authenticated actions. MCP annotations are client hints, not approvals. Tool approvals and ask-before-act hold actions for you. Approval in the client's prompt bypasses the agent; the confirm_token fallback is a second step, not proof of a human.

Approvals, user-tab protection and browser_set_policy are checks, not a sandbox: local programs with the token are not restricted.

Recommended: use a separate browser profile with only the accounts the agent needs (no banking, mail or work SSO), require approval for actions you want to see first, and treat saved sessions, screenshots and logs as sensitive. Never paste real secrets into bug reports.

docs.title: Tools
docs.text:
Every client can call every tool. There are no capability groups to configure; which tools need your approval is set in the extension's options (Your tabs and approvals). KITSUNE_SCRIPTING only chooses what tools/list advertises:

Setting tools/list Default (unset or 1) 6 code-first tools KITSUNE_SCRIPTING=0 27 core tools + 3 gateway tools

Any other value fails at startup, as do the removed KITSUNE_CAPS, KITSUNE_PUBLISH and KITSUNE_MODE. Unlisted tool names stay callable; tools/list is discovery, not an authorization boundary. browser_status reports the active surface (minimal or legacy).

docs.title: Default tools
docs.text:
• browser_run_python: reads, inputs, waits, conditions and filtering
  • browser_tabs: selection, handoff and tab lifecycle
  • browser_take_screenshot: return images to the model
  • browser_ask_user, browser_resume: ask the user for help; continue a stopped call
  • browser_tools_call: inspect or run one direct tool, for approval or recovery

browser_run_python runs trusted local Python, not a sandbox: scripts have host file and network access (Python scripting). It supplies browser and the MCP-selected tab:

tab.hover("#menu")
result = tab.snapshot(text=True)

Group only actions whose targets are already known, and return the observation the next decision needs. help(tab.hover) prints one method's signature. browser.tabs() returns dicts; wrap one with browser.tab(t["id"]).

Approvals and user-tab protection apply to script requests as to direct calls. A tool that needs approval is asked about mid-script. Other approval stops end the script without replaying completed work: the result's failed_operation.recovery_tool names a tool to call through browser_tools_call (omit arguments to see its schema; pass them to run it). Scripts cannot submit confirm_tokens and are never checkpointed.
