docs.title: Core tools
docs.text:
With KITSUNE_SCRIPTING=0, tools/list has Playwright MCP's 25 core tools, published verbatim from src/kitsune/playwright_tools.json, plus Kitsune's browser_resume and browser_ask_user. A client or prompt written for Playwright MCP works unchanged, but results are Kitsune's compact JSON. Differences:

  • Current tab. Tools act on the tab browser_tabs new or select made current. select takes any tab without switching your view; on a tab the agent cannot write, results say read_only: true. Without a current tab, reads use the active tab and writes return no_current_tab (No current tab); after a server restart that error lists the tabs this client opened in state.ownTabs. A tab opened by an action (e.g. a target=_blank click) becomes current and is named in current_tab. browser_close closes the current tab, never the browser.
  • Targets. target is a snapshot ref (e12), a CSS selector or a supported Playwright selector (Target selectors). Writes need exactly one match, else ambiguous_target. Refs stay valid while their nodes stay attached.
  • Snapshots. Inline snapshots are capped at 12,000 characters, cut between blocks, with truncated: true. Long runs of similar items collapse to … N more similar items; snapshot the container ref to list them. browser_find searches collapsed items too.
  • Sliders and keys. browser_fill_form type: "slider" sets native and ARIA sliders. browser_press_key accepts an extra repeat (1–100).
  • Dialogs. Without a policy, an agent's tab dismisses dialogs and a user's tab shows them; page actions report them in dialogs. browser_handle_dialog sets how the next dialogs are answered; one already open cannot be (dialog_open).
  • Uploads. browser_file_upload fills the file input last clicked (or the page's only one).
  • JavaScript. browser_evaluate needs the developer build.
  • Console and network. Console capture starts on first use. Network requests come from resource timing; no headers or bodies.
  • Screenshots. PNG or JPEG; scale is ignored.
  • Not supported. browser_emulate_media and browser_run_code_unsafe return not_supported.
  • File names. A relative filename resolves against KITSUNE_OUTPUT_DIR, else the client's first file:// root, else the server's working directory.

Approval holds still apply. Core schemas have no confirm_token, but the tools accept it for clients without elicitation (Approving held actions).

docs.title: Finding tools without a restart
docs.text:
On the legacy surface three gateway tools reach the unlisted tools:

  • browser_tools_search(query, limit=5): find tools with their schemas; an empty query lists all.
  • browser_tools_call(name, arguments): run one tool.
  • browser_tools_publish(names): add tools or groups to this session's tools/list.

A gateway call takes the direct call's path: the same validation, approvals, tab protection and redaction, and its audit entry records via. Your client's permission prompt may show only browser_tools_call, not the tool it runs.

Tool annotations (read-only, destructive, …) are hints for clients, not enforced policy. The bridge enforces browser_set_policy (readonly, allow/deny, ask-before-act).

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Start with browser_status: it reports a diagnosis.code and diagnosis.hint (Connection diagnosis).

docs.title: Setup and installation
docs.text: Symptom Check Server fails to start, or uvx not found Use the full path from which uvx (GUI apps). Run uvx --from kitsune-browser-mcp kitsune-bridge status in a terminal to see the error First start times out Run that status command once to fill the uv cache, then reconnect uv cannot fetch the package Check that PyPI (or your mirror) is reachable; for git+https:// sources, that git is on PATH Remove KITSUNE_CAPS from the MCP server environment Removed setting: delete it (and KITSUNE_PUBLISH, KITSUNE_MODE) from the client config A call waits, or returns needs_user with state.detail: "tool_approval" You require approval for that tool: answer in the toolbar popup, or uncheck it in the options tool_moved_to_python The default tools use browser_run_python; KITSUNE_SCRIPTING=0 restores the legacy list Upgrade not picked up Restart the client; use uvx --refresh … (Upgrading) The bridge restarts whenever another client starts Clients use different sources or refs (compatibility) "needs the developer extension build" The signed build cannot run agent JavaScript; load the developer build Stop or restart the bridge kitsune-bridge stop with the same source as your clients; the next call starts it again

docs.title: Connection
docs.text: Code Check extension_disconnected Extension enabled in the profile you opened? Developer build gone after a browser restart? It reconnects within 15 s extension_version_mismatch Install the matching extension or server, then reload tabs. stale_developer_build: reload it in about:debugging browser_window_unavailable Open a normal window, or allow Kitsune in private windows new_tab_stalled, navigation_stalled The browser cannot load pages; retrying won't help. Check browser_status(diagnostics=true) and ask the user to restart or update the browser host_permission_denied not_granted: allow site access in about:addons. restricted_domain: Mozilla sites are off-limits bridge_unavailable See state.logExcerpt and ~/.kitsune/bridge.log, or run kitsune-bridge start. not_responding: kitsune-bridge stop and retry port_conflict Another program holds the port (lsof -nP -iTCP:47651 -sTCP:LISTEN), or KITSUNE_WS_PORT differs from the extension's WS_URL token_mismatch KITSUNE_TOKEN or KITSUNE_HOME differs between client and daemon

docs.title: Tabs and approvals
docs.text: Symptom Check user_tab_read_only Nothing ran. Open the URL in an agent tab, or request a handoff needs_user, state.detail: "tab_handoff" The handoff was declined or timed out. Make a fresh request or use an agent tab needs_user, state.reason: "approval" Nothing ran. With elicitation you get a prompt; otherwise the agent repeats the call with confirm_token after you agree (Approving held actions) needs_user, state.decision: "declined" / "cancelled" Declined: don't ask again. Cancelled: browser_resume(call, resume_token) asks again needs_user, state.reason: "agent_request" The agent asked for help (sign_in, human_check, trusted_input, other); do it, then answer the prompt (When the agent needs you) browser_resume returns needs_user at once Without elicitation resume never waits for approval; approve in chat and repeat with confirm_token stale ref Take a fresh snapshot and use its refs Bridge updated, behavior unchanged Reload the extension, then the affected pages

docs.title: Pages and input
docs.text: Symptom Check Cannot access browser internal page about: pages are off-limits; use a normal tab Click dispatched but nothing happens (outcome_not_observed) The page wants trusted input. Try one browser_trusted_click and verify with a read Hover menu stays hidden Synthetic hover cannot trigger CSS :hover. Use browser_trusted_click with restore_pointer=False on a harmless element, or ask the user Press-and-hold or hover-intent control does nothing Pass hold_ms to the click or duration_ms/steps to the hover. Pointer-capturing handles need browser_trusted_drag (macOS) Hidden tab renders nothing, or hidden_or_covered with state.hiddenTab Some pages don't paint hidden tabs (Snapshot readiness). Showing the tab switches the user's view, so ask first browser_not_at_point (macOS) Another window covers the point, usually full screen on another Space or Zen's full-screen top strip. Leave full screen or scroll the target down tab_not_shown, or tabs listed as about:blank (Zen) Finish Zen's first-run welcome screen value-attribute selectors are disabled Target the sensitive field by ref or label instead "Continue with Google" opens nothing See Sign-in popups

docs.title: Sign-in popups (OAuth/SSO)
docs.text:
Firefox's popup blocker opens window.open popups only from real user input. Kitsune's clicks are synthetic, so OAuth/SSO popups are blocked or the site shows an error. When detected, the click result has a popup_blocked warning (state.reason: "script_popup") and a needs_user hint with reason: "sign_in". Two ways through:

  1. Ask the user to click (recommended). The agent calls browser_ask_user, then finds the new popup with browser_tabs.
  2. browser_trusted_click. A real OS click opens the popup, but moves your pointer and may take focus. Find the popup with browser_tabs afterwards.

docs.title: Trusted clicks
docs.text:
browser_trusted_click needs a visible browser window.

  • macOS: install a backend (uvx --from 'kitsune-browser-mcp[macos]' kitsune, or brew install cliclick), grant Accessibility permission to the app running the bridge, then run kitsune-bridge stop so the next start picks it up. The bridge uses the Python and PATH of whichever client started it, so add the extra to every client.
  • Linux: xdotool in an X11 session (not Wayland). HiDPI scaling is not compensated.

A target covered by another element returns target_not_at_point without clicking.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
Once installed, ask your agent:

Open a new tab, search for today's weather near Suseong Lake in Daegu, and summarize the forecast with a link to the source. Leave the tab open.

Or:

  • "Open Hacker News and summarize the top three stories with links."
  • "Inspect this page's form and fill a draft. Don't submit it yet."
  • "Capture a screenshot of this page and save it to a file."

A real screen recording, sped up while the agent thinks (full 38-second video).

The agent opens its own background tab first (browser_tabs new), then reads and acts on it. Writes to your tabs are refused, so it never acts on the tab you are using (Shared browser). Ask it to confirm before submitting, sending, buying or deleting. Page content is untrusted input; see Security.

To drive the browser from your own code, see the Python API.

docs.title: Your tabs and approvals
docs.text:
Every tool is available to every agent. These checks decide what it may do:

Check Covers Set in Default Protected tabs Writes to your and other clients' tabs KITSUNE_USER_TABS; per tab, a handoff Read-only Tool approvals Checked tools, also inside Python scripts and batches Extension options Cookies, storage, clipboard, sessions, history Ask-before-act Submits, payment pages, JavaScript, cookie access browser_set_policy(ask=True) or KITSUNE_ASK_BEFORE_ACT=1 Off History permission History and bookmark lookups Extension options Not granted browser_set_policy URL allow/deny lists, read-only mode The tool or bridge API No limits KITSUNE_SCRIPTING=0 Removes browser_run_python MCP server environment Python on

None of these is a sandbox: browser_run_python runs local Python with your access, and any local program with the bridge token reaches the bridge directly. See Security.

docs.title: Protecting your tabs
docs.text:
The agent can read every tab, but writes, scrolling, hovering, focusing, navigation, reload and close on your tabs (and other clients') fail at once with user_tab_read_only. The agent should open its own tab (browser_tabs action=new) instead, or ask for yours:

  • browser_tabs action=request with an index or tab_id and a reason asks for a handoff. You answer in the toolbar popup or, with elicitation, the client's prompt (up to 30 s); the first answer counts.
  • An approved tab is the agent's until you press Take back or its session ends. It allows DOM actions, not your real mouse or keyboard, and does not switch your view.

Reads don't move your view. Reads that scroll (find load_more, element or full-page screenshots) run on a protected tab only while it is not shown, and restore its scroll position. On the agent's own tabs, your input pauses writes with a retryable user_active.

KITSUNE_USER_TABS=writable lets the client write your tabs without asking (user_active and ask-before-act still apply); any value other than read-only/writable stops startup. The Python API takes kitsune.connect(user_tabs="writable") instead. See Tab permissions.

docs.title: When the agent needs you
docs.text: For a sign-in, CAPTCHA or a button that ignores synthetic clicks, results carry a needs_user hint (sign_in, human_check, trusted_input). When the agent cannot go on it calls browser_ask_user: answer Accept when done or Decline in the client's prompt, or in chat on clients without elicitation. For a sign-in or CAPTCHA, browser_resume waits until it is gone (details).

docs.title: Tools that need your approval
docs.text:
In about:addons → Kitsune → Options, check the tools that should wait for your OK. storage and history tools are checked by default; browser_run_python is not.

A checked call shows a card in the toolbar popup (and the client's prompt, with elicitation):

  • Allow once runs that call.
  • Allow for this session allows that client's later calls until the bridge restarts.
  • Decline leaves it unrun.

The check also applies inside browser_run_python scripts and batch or workflow steps. Your own Python API scripts are not asked.

docs.title: Ask-before-act
docs.text:
An opt-in policy that holds form submits, submit/payment-like buttons ("Place order", "결제하기"), Enter in form fields, agent JavaScript, cookie/session/storage access, clipboard, downloads, and payment-like URLs until you approve (details).

  • browser_set_policy(ask=True): the agent can turn it off again, so it only guards accidents.
  • Locked: KITSUNE_ASK_BEFORE_ACT=1 or kitsune-bridge start --ask-before-act. It writes ~/.kitsune/ask-before-act-locked, and every bridge starts locked while that file exists. To unlock, remove the variable, delete the file and run kitsune-bridge stop.
[mcp_servers.kitsune.env]
KITSUNE_ASK_BEFORE_ACT = "1"

The target is checked before acting; a page that changes in between (e.g. navigates to checkout) is not caught.

docs.title: Approving held actions
docs.text:
A held call returns needs_user with state.reason: "approval" and does not run.

  • Clients with elicitation (Claude Code, Codex) ask you in their prompt with the action, target and tab. Approve runs that one call; the agent never sees a token. Declined or dismissed calls return state.decision declined or cancelled; browser_resume asks again. Batch and workflow steps are not asked about: the agent repeats the step as a direct call.
  • Other clients get a single-use confirm_token (120 s, bound to the exact action). The agent should ask you, then repeat the call with it. The agent can do this without asking, so it guards only against accidents; have your client prompt you before tool calls.

The audit log (browser_audit) records each approval as elicitation or token (Approval prompts).
